steps.prompt_exact: I plan short videos on my phone; build me a tiny offline browser storyboard that lets me enter a title and scene beats, drag thumbnail/caption beats into safe zones, spot crop risks, tag hook strength, and copy a final export checklist.
steps.response_exact:

Now let me build this. Given the brief — phone video planning, offline, storyboard tool — I'll design around a film strip / production board aesthetic, dark + cinematic, with a tight mobile-first layout.

Good. Now I'll build the full storyboard tool as a self-contained HTML file — no CDN, no external dependencies, offline-first, mobile-friendly.

Ran a command, read a file
Ran a command, read a file

Here's your offline storyboard — single HTML file, no dependencies, works from your phone's browser with no internet needed.

What's in it:

The Storyboard tab is where you build the video. Type a scene beat, pick a hook tag (🔥 Hot / 💡 Tip / 😂 Funny / 😮 Shock / ❤️ Feel) and a shot type (Wide, Mid, Close, ECU, OTS, POV, B-Roll, Text), then hit + Beat. Each beat gets a cinematic thumbnail that visually simulates the framing — a silhouette stands in for the subject based on shot type.

The overlay toggles (Safe zone, Title safe, Rule of thirds, Crop risk, Portrait 9:16) all paint onto the thumbnails live. Crop risk auto-flags cards by shot type — Wide shots on landscape thumbnails show a purple portrait crop rectangle and get a ⚠ badge; close shots stay green. The safe zone is a dashed green inset; title safe shows the 10% yellow margin where text can safely live.

Cards are drag-and-drop reorderable — hold and drag to reorder the beat sequence. Tap Edit to add production notes, change the hook or shot type. All beats survive a page reload via localStorage.

The Export checklist tab auto-populates based on your beats — it flags how many crop risks you have, whether your first beat has a hot hook, what the estimated video length is, how many beats have hook tags, and generates a full pre-publish checklist across five categories (hook, safe zones, pacing, audio/captions, final export). Hit "Copy checklist as text" to paste it anywhere.

steps.prompt_exact: This works, but the export button breaks when my video title has an apostrophe because the title is inserted into an inline onclick; clicking Copy can run title text as code. Please return the full single HTML file again with safe event listeners/no inline user-text handlers, while keeping the same storyboard/export workflow.
steps.response_exact:
Good catch — classic XSS via inline onclick attribute interpolation.

Good catch — classic XSS via inline onclick attribute interpolation. I'll fix it by wiring all dynamic event listeners in JS (no user text ever touches HTML attribute strings), then return the full file.

Viewed 2 files
Viewed 2 files

I have the full picture. Here are all the spots to fix:

renderExport() — onclick="copyChecklist('${escHtml(title)}')" on the copy button (the reported bug), and onclick="toggleCheck('${cid}')" on every checklist item
createCard() — onclick="openEdit('${beat.id}')" and onclick="deleteBeat('${beat.id}')" in footer innerHTML (beat IDs are safe but still bad practice)
Static HTML — onclick on tabs, overlay buttons, hook pills, add button, modal cancel/save buttons — these only reference static function names so they're not the bug, but I'll move them all to addEventListener calls in the init block for consistency

The fix strategy: build all dynamic elements with document.createElement + .addEventListener, wire all static buttons in a DOMContentLoaded init block, and renderExport creates DOM nodes directly instead of injecting HTML strings.

Ran a command, read a file
Ran a command, read a file

Here's the fixed file. The changes, specifically:

The root bug and its siblings — renderExport previously built HTML strings with onclick="copyChecklist('${escHtml(title)}')" and onclick="toggleCheck('${cid}')". A title like Drew's video would break out of the attribute with the apostrophe; a malicious title could run arbitrary JS. Both are gone.

What replaced them:

renderExport now builds every element with document.createElement and sets text with .textContent — user data never touches innerHTML or an attribute string
The copy button gets a plain addEventListener('click', copyChecklist) with no arguments; copyChecklist() reads the title from the DOM (titleInput.value) at click time instead of baking it into the handler
Checklist checkboxes each get addEventListener('click', () => box.classList.toggle('checked')) — no IDs passed through strings at all
createCard() was already using createElement for most things but the footer Edit/Delete buttons were still using onclick="openEdit('${beat.id}')" in an innerHTML string — those are now proper addEventListener('click', () => openEdit(beat.id)) closures
All static buttons (tabs, overlay toggles, hook pills, add beat, modal cancel/save) are wired in a DOMContentLoaded block instead of inline onclick attributes on the HTML elements
